pending.title: OPM final rule replaces seniority/tenure-protective RIF procedures with performance-based retention criteria
pending.rationale: Final OPM rule (published, not proposed) restructures reduction-in-force procedures to prioritize performance ratings over tenure and length of service, removing a longstanding seniority-based safeguard against politicized personnel decisions. This is a confirmed, executed regulatory action creating a durable mechanism for at-will-style workforce reshaping within RIF actions, distinct from the broader Schedule Policy/Career reclassification already on the ledger. Scope is targeted to RIF procedures, warranting magnitude 2.

pending.title: OPM final rule strips MSPB jurisdiction over suitability action appeals, consolidating review authority within OPM
pending.rationale: Final OPM rule removes the independent Merit Systems Protection Board from adjudicating suitability action appeals and consolidates that authority inside the executive personnel office itself. This eliminates an external check on the executive's use of suitability determinations to screen or remove federal personnel, a durable structural change confirmed via Federal Register final-rule publication. Effect is contained to suitability appeals, meriting magnitude 2 rather than higher.

pending.title: OPM final rule streamlines probationary and trial-period employee appeals, curtailing procedural review
pending.rationale: A separate, final OPM regulation published 2026-08-03 narrows appeal rights specifically for probationary and trial-period federal employees, distinct from the already-pending RIF performance-based rule and the MSPB suitability-appeals rule. This is a confirmed, durable regulatory change targeting a specific class of employees' procedural protections, warranting its own ledger entry at a targeted-scope magnitude (2).

pending.title: Supreme Court allows enforcement of executive order restricting mail-in voting without statutory authorization
pending.rationale: The Supreme Court declined to block and thereby allowed enforcement of an executive order imposing restrictions on mail-in voting nationwide, an action taken without congressional authorization. This is a confirmed, durable structural change: the order can now take legal effect, shifting authority over a facet of election administration from statute/state control to unilateral executive action. Scope is limited to mail-in voting mechanics rather than full federal takeover of election administration, warranting a targeted-scope magnitude rather than a broader one.

pending.title: MSPB final rule eliminates Douglas factors proportionality test for federal employee misconduct penalties
pending.rationale: A final MSPB rule, effective upon Federal Register publication, removes the longstanding multi-factor proportionality review (Douglas factors) that previously constrained agency discretion in selecting misconduct penalties, including removal. This is a completed, durable legal change (not a proposal) that weakens a specific procedural check on politicized or arbitrary dismissals across the federal misconduct-adjudication process, though it is narrow in scope (limited to penalty-selection review) and does not itself demonstrate a mass removal campaign underway.
